note: Framingham: 2 major or 1 major + 2 minor criteria. Available: paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (major); ankle oedema and dyspnoea on exertion (minor); orthopnoea (added from ESC 2021). Signs and imaging are not available.
WHO: measured fever >= 38 C and cough with onset within 10 days; DDXPlus records felt or measured fever and no onset date.
DSM-5 requires >= 4 of 13 symptoms in an abrupt surge; trembling and fear of losing control are not asked, so 11 items are available.
ECG and troponin, which separate NSTEMI/STEMI from unstable angina, are not available.
Sampson: >= 2 of skin-mucosa, respiratory compromise, reduced blood pressure, persistent GI symptoms, rapidly after a likely allergen; onset timing is not asked.
Mackler's triad: vomiting, lower thoracic pain and subcutaneous emphysema; emphysema is an examination finding.
ICHD-3 3.1 also requires unilateral attacks of 15-180 min, >= 5 attacks; laterality, duration and attack count are not asked.
EPOS requires symptoms for >= 12 weeks; duration is not asked.
WHO lists headache, vomiting, anorexia, diarrhoea, lethargy, stomach pain, aching muscles or joints, difficulty swallowing, breathing difficulty and hiccup; hiccup is not asked.
Two-tier Wells: PE likely if > 4 points. Heart rate > 100 (+1.5) and 'PE the most likely diagnosis' (+3) cannot be scored, so the score is a lower bound.
ESC: typical pain is sharp, pleuritic, improved by sitting up and leaning forward; rub, ECG and effusion criteria need examination.
The CDC clinical criteria also require a cough of >= 2 weeks; duration is not asked.
The entry criterion (ANA >= 1:80) needs a laboratory test.
Typical angina has three characteristics: constricting retrosternal discomfort, provoked by exertion, relieved by rest or nitrates within 5 min. The 5-minute relief and nitrates are not asked.
Cough duration (>= 2 weeks) and night sweats are not asked as such; 'significantly increased sweating' is the closest question.
Wells: clinical signs and symptoms of DVT (leg swelling and pain on palpation of the deep veins); DDXPlus records only the swelling site.
Blood pressure is not measured in DDXPlus; near-syncope and syncope are the associated end-organ symptoms named by Sampson.
Jaundice is examined, not asked; pale stools with dark urine and a yellow skin colour stand in for it.
